title: Incremental Even-Weighted Cycle Queries
summary: Given a positive integer n, you have an undirected graph with n nodes labeled from 0 to n-1 and initially no edges.
statement: Given a positive integer n, you have an undirected graph with n nodes labeled from 0 to n-1 and initially no edges. You are provided with a 2D integer array edges, where each edge is defined by [ui, vi, wi], connecting nodes ui and vi with a weight wi that is either 0 or 1. Process each edge in the order given, adding it to the graph only if the sum of the weights of the edges in every cycle in the graph remains even after the addition. Return the count of edges successfully added to the graph.
constraints: Nodes are 0 through n-1 and each edge weight is zero or one.
Process edges in order, accepting an edge only when every cycle in the accepted graph has even weight sum.
hints: All cycles have even weight sum exactly when vertices admit binary potentials with p[u] xor p[v]=edge weight.
Maintain those relative potentials in a parity union-find.
An intra-component edge is accepted only if its required parity matches; a merging edge sets the child-root parity consistently.
The potential equations imply even XOR around every cycle, and any odd cycle produces the detected contradiction.
editorial: The potential equations imply even XOR around every cycle, and any odd cycle produces the detected contradiction.
